title: Route a cable between two posts and secure its final clip
instruction: Use both grippers to route the orange wire between the two metal posts and seat it in the blue clip. Keep it retained in the green clip throughout. Finish with the connected wire span passing through the marked gap below the post tops, both clips seated, and both hands released and clear.
context: Preserve an existing cable fixing while routing its connected span through a guide and securing the next fixing.
setup: Two YAM arms on the calibrated station, bases 610 mm apart, with an 1100 x 1300 mm wooden table at z=747.5 mm. Coordinates are millimetres, x forward and y toward the left arm from the midpoint between bases. A fixed dark metal plate, 400 x 510 x 8 mm, is centred at (270,80) with top z=755.5 mm. Two fixed metal posts, diameter 20 mm and height 55 mm, stand at (320,0) and (320,100); the clear gap is 80 mm. A pale 36 x 80 mm painted stripe marks the passage. Green and blue polymer clip housings, 44 x 44 x 3 mm, are centred at (200,225) and (370,-50) on the plate. Each has two 6 g passive sliding jaws with rounded 2.2 mm lip radii, 4 mm travel, spring stiffness 650 N/m and damping 1 N s/m. The orange insulated wire is 8 mm diameter, 545 mm centreline length and 87.2 g, represented by 46 rounded capsule links with passive bend springs. It starts retained in the green clip, with a slack loop entirely upstream of x=320 mm and its free end near (311,-104) after settling; the blue clip is empty. Both hands start open at (220,+/-260,960). No loose objects besides the wire. Geometry and exact authored reset poses are in geometry.py/task.py; the screenshot is the post-settling start.
scoring: Any loss of green retention (mid-plane crossing x offset <12 mm and height -1..22.5 mm above its base) or a wire-joint gap >3 mm irreversibly gives 0. Missing or invalid native measurements invalidate the trial. Otherwise 0.5 requires both arms to have simultaneous fingertip/wire contact for at least 0.2 s while a blue mid-plane crossing is within 15 mm in x and 0..80 mm high; blue alignment within 8 mm in x and 4..50 mm high; and correct routing. Only the ordered connected span from the first seated green crossing to the following aligned or seated blue crossing counts. It must cross x=320 mm at least once, with every crossing centreline at y=14..86 mm and 3..51 mm above the plate. For 1.0, both clips must additionally be seated (mid-plane x offset <2 mm and height 4..12 mm), with no robot/wire contact, both TCPs >70 mm from every wire-link centre and every link moving <30 mm/s. Hold these full-score conditions for 2 seconds (40 controls). All other outcomes score 0. Routing is assessed at the endpoint; passing above a post earlier is allowed. The runtime retains the latest sub-full score during the success hold.
run_limit: 1200 controls at 20 Hz (60 simulated seconds), including the 2-second full-score hold. The scripted demo continues through final observation.
fidelity: Native Isaac Sim/PhysX. The wire uses 46 capsule bodies with passive bending springs and locked axial twist. Sliding spring jaws approximate flexible clip arms. Contact alone moves and retains the wire; no grasp attachments or object animation. Mass, stiffness, friction and damping are uncalibrated. Conductor strain, wear, electrical behavior and damage are omitted. The scripted controller reads privileged state; two-arm participation is explicitly scored.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.0 after 1200 controls; careful scripted demo: 1.0 after 1184 controls. Dream: 25 chunks, 49 API attempts, 24 session renewals; renewed-session evaluation. The demo has zero inter-arm and robot/post touch substeps.
reset_notes: Seed 0, no jitter. Restore authored wire, clip jaws and open hands; settle 0.5 s. Require green retention, blue empty, joint gaps <=2 mm and wire above the plate before scoring. No consumables. Exact authored poses and reset validation are in geometry.py/task.py. Reproduce the task through its Python runner; the exported USD is for inspection.
